transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I, um… I’m probably making it sound worse than it is, but I’ve been hearing things at work. Like voices coming through the call-light speaker, and sometimes the hallway vents. They’ll say which patient records have been changed, and it sounds really clear—like someone is standing right next to me—even when the unit is quiet.

I know that sounds… not good. But nobody else seems to hear it, so I thought I should come in and talk to someone.
Have you used any drugs recently?
No, not really. I mean… I don’t use drugs, if that’s what you mean. I’m not trying to hide anything—I know you have to ask. I just don’t do that stuff.
Have you had a period recently where you felt unusually energized or elated?

A little, yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it “elated,” exactly. Some days I just feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see what needs fixing at work and I’m meant to handle it. It feels productive at the time.

But then if my husband, or one of the nurses, tells me to slow down, I… I can get really sharp with them. Like they’re getting in the way of something important. I’m not proud of that. Does that make sense?
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling rested?

I’m not sure… I mean, my sleep hasn’t been perfect, but I don’t know that I’d say I need much less and feel rested. Some nights I toss around, but I’m not sure if it’s enough to count as that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had any recent seizures?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t had anything like that, at least not that I’m aware of. If there’s something specific you mean by seizure, you can tell me, but I don’t think I’ve had one.
During this time, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not most of the day nearly every day. I mean, I have off days, and I can get discouraged, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really been noticing that kind of constant depressed feeling, if that’s what you mean.
Do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or monitor you?

I don’t want to sound dramatic or paranoid, but… yes, a little. At work, with the wound-care charts, I know there’s a pattern there that management doesn’t want people noticing. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, but I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it. Does that make sense?
How long have you been hearing the voices?

I guess… about two months? It started around when they asked me to help lead the wound-care documentation rollout. I didn’t really think of it as “hearing voices” at first, but that’s about when I noticed it. Is that the kind of timing you mean?
During the time you've been hearing the voices, have there been several days in a row when you felt unusually high or irritable most of the day?

Yes… I think there have been stretches like that. I don’t know if I’d call it “high” exactly, but some days I feel like I’m finally awake, like I’m supposed to fix everything at work. And then if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I… I snap at them, more than I should, like they’re getting in the way of something important. Is that what you mean?
Was there ever a time when the voices were happening but your mood was otherwise normal?

I don’t think so… not that I can remember. The call-light voices and the messages in the charts, that all started after I was already kind of wound up about the rollout — sleeping less, working constantly, feeling like I had to fix everything at the facility.

Before that, I mean, I was stressed, but I wasn’t hearing things like that. Does that answer what you’re asking?
During this period, was there a time when your mood felt unusually elevated or irritable most of the day for at least one full week?

Yes… I think so. There was at least a week where most of the day I felt sort of… energized, like I was finally awake and I was meant to fix everything at work. I didn’t think of it as a problem at the time.

But I was also more irritable than I want to admit. If my husband or one of the nurses told me to slow down, I’d snap at them, like they were blocking something important. That sounds like what you’re asking, right?
During that week when you felt unusually energized or irritable, were you hospitalized because of it?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I don’t think I should say yes if I’m not certain. I remember people being worried about me, but whether I was actually hospitalized because of that week… I don’t want to give you the wrong information.

Is it okay if I say I’m not sure?
During that week, did your symptoms make it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Yes… I mean, I hate saying that, but yes. I was still trying really hard to do my job, but my supervisor took me off the floor during a shift because she said my handoffs and charting weren’t safe anymore.

And at home, my husband has had to pick up things I normally handle. I keep wanting to say it wasn’t that bad, but… it was affecting things. I feel like my reputation at work is kind of falling apart, and I’m worried I’ve ruined my chances for LPN school. Is that the kind of functioning you mean?
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices but were not feeling unusually energized, high, or irritable?

No… I don’t think so. The voices from the call lights, and feeling like there were messages hidden in the charts — that didn’t happen before I got so wound up about the rollout.

It started after I was barely sleeping and working nonstop, and I felt so sure I had to fix everything at the facility. So I don’t remember a separate two-week stretch where that was happening and I wasn’t also energized or irritable. Does that answer it okay?
